executive_summary: The dominant thread unifying today's news is the intensifying friction between institutional governance, political accountability, and systemic restructuring across American life. This theme is vividly highlighted in the breaking news by the Senate confirmation of Jay Clayton to lead the intelligence community alongside contentious congressional inquiries involving Anthony Fauci and Donald Trump. Foreign Affairs newsletters reinforce this trajectory by examining America's strategic push to reindustrialize and leverage its energy advantages against global rivals like Beijing. Simultaneously, MIT Technology Review demonstrates how corporate talent migration at Samsung mirrors these fierce competitive pressures within the global technology sector. Together, these developments signal a pivotal moment where institutional stability is continually tested by domestic political maneuverings and international economic rivalry.

items.headline: Crispy bean cakes with harissa, lemon and herbs
items.blurb: Two things in particular about this Yewande Komolafe recipe speak to me. First, I love that it calls for two cans of pretty much any canned bean you have on hand (or any that’s on sale) — black-eyed peas, chickpeas, pinto, kidney or black beans would all work. And second, I can’t shake the thought that these golden, just-spicy-enough little patties would make for excellent bean burgers, either as sliders on Hawaiian rolls or as larger patties on potato buns with some quick cabbage slaw.

items.headline: Chilled cucumber noodles
items.blurb: “A base of cucumber broth is made by blending cucumbers, stirring in ice and seasoning simply with vinegar and sugar.” That’s from the headnote of this new Sue Li recipe, and just reading it makes my shoulders relax and my mouth water.

items.headline: Anda bhurji (tomato-chile scrambled eggs)
items.blurb: When I’m tired and lazy but still want to eat something that’s good for me, I always remember: tomato eggs. Tomato eggs take many forms (shakshuka; Chinese stir-fried tomatoes and eggs; huevos rancheros), including these spiced scrambled eggs, known in South Asia as anda bhurji. Zainab Shah’s recipe needs just a handful of pantry standbys — garlic, ginger, a shallot or onion, chile powder — to come together in 20 minutes.

newsletters.title: The US in Brief: Trump’s approval rating hits a new low

items.headline: Trump's approval rating hits a new low
items.blurb: Donald Trump’s net approval rating fell to a record low of -25, according to The Economist’s tracker of YouGov polling. The administration’s resumption of strikes on Iran in mid-July might be to blame. The war remains deeply unpopular with most Americans. Our polling suggests that 60% of them think the administration is spending too much money on the conflict.

items.headline: Attempted surprise attack on US forces
items.blurb: Meanwhile, US Central Command said that Iran had launched an “attempted surprise attack” on its forces in the Middle East. It added that it had intercepted ballistic missiles. The attack represents the end of a pause in fighting between the countries in recent days. America also said it had joined forces with Saudi Arabia to bomb “Iran-backed terrorist sites” in Iraq.

items.headline: Senate confirms Jay Clayton
items.blurb: The Senate confirmed the nomination of Jay Clayton as director of national intelligence in a 51-47 vote. Democrats voted against the nomination after Mr Clayton refused to say whether Joe Biden won the 2020 election during his confirmation hearing. Still, lawmakers from both parties consider him a better option to oversee America’s intelligence agencies than Mr Trump’s first pick, Bill Pulte.

items.headline: Sanctions on Russia and Iran advanced
items.blurb: Senators also advanced a bill that would tighten sanctions on Russia and Iran, and allow tariffs on countries which buy Russian oil and gas. The legislation was co-authored by Lindsey Graham, a Republican senator from South Carolina who died on July 11th. Israel’s prime minister, Binyamin Netanyahu, and Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelensky, attended Mr Graham’s funeral in Washington on Tuesday before separately meeting Mr Trump.

items.headline: Todd Blanche's nomination could be postponed
items.blurb: John Cornyn, a Republican senator from Texas, said that a committee vote to advance Todd Blanche’s nomination for attorney-general, expected this week, could be postponed. Senators are concerned by Mr Blanche’s role in the proposed creation of a $1.8bn fund to pay people whom Mr Trump says have been unfairly investigated by the government. Mr Blanche previously told senators that the plan is “dead”. Mr Cornyn wants that confirmed in writing before advancing the nomination.
